stories.title: Dell Launches Unified Semantic Layer, Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents for Enterprise AI
stories.body: Dell expanded its AI Data Platform on October 6, 2026, shipping three new capabilities: a Unified Semantic Layer, an Enterprise Knowledge Graph, and Knowledge Agents — designed to give AI agents a shared, governed understanding of company data. The semantic layer resolves terminology conflicts across systems (e.g., 'client' vs. 'account'), while the knowledge graph maps how those entities connect, enabling agents to reason across domains rather than within siloed datasets. The announcement is a direct infrastructure commitment: Dell is betting that agents fail without this context foundation, not because of model limitations.
stories.why: This is the exact architecture argument Graas makes on every discovery call — agents hallucinate without a semantic context layer, and the problem is data, not the model. A named vendor shipping this stack in October 2026 gives sellers a third-party proof point that the context layer is now table stakes, not a nice-to-have.

stories.title: Gartner + Forrester: 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by 2027; 88% of Pilots Never Reach Production
stories.body: Gartner's standing forecast — based on a poll of 3,400+ organizations — predicts more than 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by end of 2027, killed by escalating costs, unclear business value, and inadequate risk controls, not model failure. A 2026 Forrester study run with Anaconda sharpens the picture further: 88% of AI agent pilots never reach production, with evaluation gaps (64%), governance friction (57%), and model reliability (51%) as the leading blockers. McKinsey's August 2026 State of AI survey separately found only about 20% of organizations have scaled agents in any function.
stories.why: This is the single most powerful objection-handling asset a Graas seller has: when a prospect says 'we're piloting internally,' these numbers show why pilots stall — it is the data and governance foundation that fails, exactly the gap Graas addresses. Cite Gartner's 40% figure and the Forrester 88% figure together to reframe build-vs-buy conversations.

stories.tag: US - named CPG enterprise deployment with outcomes
stories.title: BCG May 2026 Report: GenAI Supply Chain Agents Deliver +2–4% In-Stock Lift, +4–10% Fill Rate, and 40–60% Admin Savings at Global CPG Leader
stories.body: BCG's May 2026 Executive Perspectives report on supply chain documents a named engagement at a global CPG company where GenAI-enabled agents shifted replenishment from reactive to proactive — delivering smart DC-to-store transfer recommendations and expedited order triggers via a human-in-the-loop feedback loop. Measured outcomes: +2–4 percentage points in in-stock rate driving revenue lift, +4–10% fill rate improvement, and 40–60% administrative savings for the planning team. The agent back end was built modularly for future expansion across additional workflows.
stories.why: This is the proof-of-outcome story sellers need for supply chain and replenishment conversations with large CPG and grocery accounts. The BCG authorship adds credibility, and the outcome numbers (in-stock, fill rate, admin savings) map directly to the KPIs retail ops and supply chain buyers measure — making this usable as a leave-behind or talk track anchor.

stories.title: Decagon Crosses $100M ARR in August 2026, Betting Against Forward-Deployed Engineers
stories.body: Decagon disclosed in August 2026 that annualized revenue had crossed $100 million — up from an estimated $44 million at end of 2025, representing roughly 3x year-over-year growth — reaching this milestone three years after founding. The company reached $100M ARR while deliberately avoiding the forward-deployed engineer model used by rivals like Sierra, with CEO Jesse Zhang emphasizing speed and self-serve product design as the differentiator. Decagon's enterprise customer base spans F100 companies across airlines, banks, telecom, and retail, including Avis Budget Group and Mercado Libre, with per-resolution and subscription hybrid pricing typically negotiated in the tens of thousands of dollars per month.
stories.why: Decagon is a direct competitor in enterprise customer-service agent deals, and its $100M ARR milestone signals that the market for standalone AI agent layers is real and scaling fast. Sellers need to know Decagon's 'no forward-deployed engineers' pitch — it is how they win fast land deals — and understand that its pricing model (per resolution + platform fee) sets the benchmark buyers will use to evaluate Graas on cost-per-outcome.

stories.title: Salesforce Completes $3.6B Acquisition of Fin (Formerly Intercom), Folds It Into Agentforce
stories.body: Salesforce completed its acquisition of Fin — the AI customer-service agent business formerly known as Intercom — on September 10, 2026, paying approximately $3.6 billion and folding Fin into its Agentforce platform. The deal was framed by Salesforce as a direct bid to own the AI customer-service category before vertical agent startups like Sierra and Decagon capture enterprise budgets. Fin continues to publish $0.99 per resolved conversation pricing, now with the full Salesforce CRM and data stack behind it — a combination that changes the competitive surface for any standalone agent vendor in accounts already on Salesforce.
stories.why: Any enterprise retail account already on Salesforce CRM is now a potential Fin/Agentforce cross-sell target, which means Graas will encounter a bundled incumbent in more deals. Sellers need to understand the pricing ($0.99/resolution vs. Sierra's ~$1.50 estimate) and the key weakness: bundled tools inherit Salesforce's data model, meaning the same context-layer gaps Graas solves still exist unless the customer has clean, governed product and order data.
